name: GoldenEye
tagline: Beach villas, lagoon cottages and huts on Oracabessa Bay.
description:
GoldenEye is a collection of villas, cottages and beach huts on Oracabessa Bay, in the parish of St. Mary, Jamaica, and it belongs to Island Outpost. In 1946 Ian Fleming bought 15 acres in Oracabessa, a former donkey racetrack, and named the house GoldenEye. He created the James Bond character while there. Chris Blackwell, founder of Island Records, acquired the property in the 1970s and added huts, cottages and villas.

Five one-bedroom beach villas and four two-bedroom beach villas open onto Low Cay Beach, 500 feet of sand in a croissant shape. A three-bedroom beach villa adds a detached third bedroom and a stone deck onto the lagoon. Lagoon cottages face Santa Maria Island, a small uninhabited island in a four-acre lagoon, and each has a private dock and a kayak. Villa Vesper is a five-bedroom house on that lagoon, with king bedrooms, an open-plan kitchen and verandas. Strangways is a three-bedroom compound on a bluff, with a butler, a master structure, two further bedroom structures and a separate kitchen, and stone steps down to the lagoon. Spanish Elm is a one-bedroom lagoon hut from the first buildings, with a kitchenette and a terrace. Some beach huts are raised ten feet, with the bedroom above and an open-air lounge below, between the gardens of Snorkeler's Cove and Button Beach. Architect Ann Hodges designed the villas, with hardwood floors, outdoor showers and full kitchens.

Bizot Bar sits on the western arm of Low Cay Beach beside the freshwater pool and serves breakfast and lunch, including Jamaican dishes. Button Beach Bar and Grill cooks jerk and fish from local boats. Shabeen, by the beach huts, serves cocktails and has a rooftop lounge. Meals can also be taken in the room or on a veranda.

The spa is a cottage on the edge of the lagoon, with treatment rooms open to the air. Botanicals are drawn from Pantrepant, an Island Outpost farm. On the water, Low Cay is the main beach and Button Beach has a bar shack. Kayaks and paddleboards are part of the day, and a visit can be arranged to Firefly, the house Noel Coward built.

Ian Fleming International Airport at Boscobel is 2.7 miles away, less than a 10-minute drive. Sangster International in Montego Bay is 73 miles, about 1 hour and 45 minutes. Norman Manley in Kingston is 57 miles, less than 2 hours. Ocho Rios is about 20 minutes away.
